text: Upton Sinclair's The Jungle was banned from public libraries in Yugoslavia in 1929 for its socialist views. Nazi students burned the book in Germany in 1933 because of Sinclair's socialist views. In 1953 Senator Joe McCarthy scrutinized it for its Communist sympathies, and in 1956 it was banned in East Germany as inimical to communism. It was banned in South Korea in 1985 for Sinclair's socialist views.
meta_description: Upton Sinclair's The Jungle: banned in Yugoslavia (1929), burned in Germany (1933), banned in East Germany (1956) and South Korea (1985) over its politics.
